sense: let him …, let them …: an order or wish for someone else

terms.gloss: let him come, let it be
terms.grammar: the present subjunctive, third person; negative nē
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.118: aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat
Mart. 2.90.10: sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs
terms.comment: One mood gives orders and wishes alike: “let him drink”, “may the night bring sleep”. The negative is nē. “Let me …”, asking leave, is sine (see allow); “let’s” has its own record.

terms.gloss: so be it, all right; let it be done
terms.comment: The everyday assent of comedy, and the word of creation.

evidence: Cic. Div. Caec. 47: estō: ipse nihil est, nihil potest (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Cicerō meus quid aget? iste vērō sit in sinū semper et complexū meō
phrases.english: What will my little Cicero do? Let him be always in my lap and in my arms.

phrases.latin: sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs
phrases.english: let the night come with sleep, the day without quarrels

phrases.latin: Ī sōdēs intrō; cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter. — Fīat.
phrases.english: Do go in; I’ll follow you in a moment, mother. — Very well.

phrases.latin: Dīxitque Deus: Fīat lūx. Et facta est lūx.
phrases.english: And God said, Let there be light. And there was light.
